criticAssessment:
Coverage is honestly strong: all 15 subsystems were audited and 6 cross-cutters run, producing ~120 confirmed findings that touch the central files of every subsystem (Runner, State, Handlers, IPC, Composer stack, resources, DB layer, command families). I verified line counts to separate true blind spots from merely-uncited-but-covered files. Four genuine gaps remain worth a second finder pass:

1. DB command cluster (db.pm, db/importer, db/publish, db/recent, db/sweeper, list, recent, server) — 8 tiny (36-59 line) recently-added command files that NO finding cited; the db-layer pass hit Connect/Logger/ORM/Sync/Schema but not these command bodies, which likely inter-duplicate and duplicate import.pm/client/*.

2. Six substantial standalone commands (reload/do/init/which/help ~100 exec lines each, projects ~227) never cited by the command-boilerplate cross-cutter — real code bodies unexamined for dead imports, dead slots, and shared Pfile/client boilerplate.

3. Error-handling consistency — a named, mandated repo dimension (the `my $ok=eval{...;1}; my $err=$@` rule) that was only ever incidentally cited once (CoverageAggregator); ~61 eval sites in lib/ were never systematically checked for $@-clobber, silent swallow, or newline-less die.

4. The stream/event reader-producer layer (RunnerReader, JobReader, RenderLoop/Producer, JSONLFileProducer) — a suspicious cross-subsystem set doing parallel JSONL read-decode-dispatch work that was never compared; only LiveProducer inside it got findings.

Everything else (parallel Util/UUID/Composer modules, process-spawn duplication, socket/IPC code, render stack, options plugins) is already well-covered by confirmed findings, so I stopped at four rather than manufacturing marginal passes.

confirmedFindings.title: Canonical Composer contains unreachable/broken render plumbing: nonexistent halt()/render_times() handlers, dead Data::Dumper $msg blocks, shadowed $type
confirmedFindings.evidence: (1) Composer.pm:23 `return (($class->halt($f))[0]) if $class->{control} && ...` — the invocant is either a class name or the empty hash blessed in new() (line 12, `bless({}, $class)`); no code ever sets a `control` key on the composer, so the condition can never be true (it plainly means `$f->{control}`), and if it ever fired it would crash: `grep -n 'sub halt' lib/Test2/Formatter/Test2/Composer.pm` finds no halt() method. (2) Line 25 dispatch list `qw/assert errors plan info times about/` builds `render_times` (line 27 `my $m = "render_$type"`) — no render_times exists in the file or anywhere in lib/reference (grep -rn 'sub render_times' lib reference is empty), so any facet_data carrying a top-level `times` key on the one-line path is a method-not-found crash; relatedly Test2.pm:569 pops a `'times'` component that no code in the dist emits (grep -rn "'times'" lib matches only that line). (3) render_info (276-289) and render_errors (313-329) each compute `$msg` via Data::Dumper/chomp then push `$details` instead — `$msg` is never read; the two blocks are also copy-pastes of each other. (4) render_about 299-304: `my $type; if (...) { my $type = $f->{about}->{package}; $type =~ s/^.*:://; } $type //= 'ABOUT';` — the inner `my` shadows the outer, so the package-derived tag is always discarded and the tag is always ABOUT.
confirmedFindings.proposal: Delete the line-23 halt branch and drop `times` from the dispatch list (or implement render_times if the facet is real for Test2-Collector events); either use `$msg` as the rendered details in render_info/render_errors (restoring the evident intent of dumping ref payloads) or delete the dumper blocks and share one details-normalizer between the two subs; remove the inner `my` in render_about so the package tag works.
confirmedFindings.accuracy_note: Corrections/context that temper the proposal without refuting it: (a) All four defects are inherited verbatim from the human-authored references — reference/pre_ai_2.0/lib/App/Yath/Renderer/Default/Composer.pm and reference/legacy (shipped CPAN 1.x) have the identical line 23, `times` dispatch entry, unused $msg blocks, and shadowed $type — so these are decade-old upstream quirks faithfully ported, not regressions from the 2.0 rewrite; fixing them intentionally diverges from the canonical reference port. (b) Line 23 is worse than merely dead: because $class->{control} on a string invocant dies under strict refs, calling render_one_line as a class method (the calling convention the module's own POD advertises: "All methods are class methods") crashes for any event lacking a `render` facet; only the instance-based caller in Test2.pm avoids this. (c) The two Composer files are NOT pure copies: App::Yath2::Renderer::Default::Composer differs at line 195 (extra `$_->{peek}` in the render_brief info grep) and line 242 (undef-safe amnesty dedup key `map { $_ // '' }`); the cited line ranges are identical in both, but any dedup/cleanup must preserve those two divergences. (d) On branch 2.0d the Default::Composer currently has no live callers at all — its consumers (Schema/RunProcessor, Schema/Overlay/Event) were moved to reference/old_db in commit 647b55466 pending the DB rewrite — so fixes there affect nothing until the db-rewrite branch re-adopts it. (e) render_info vs render_errors: only the ~10-line Dumper block is a copy-paste; the surrounding subs materially differ (table passthrough and `// ''` in info vs tag/FATAL fallback in errors), so "share one normalizer" should mean extracting just the ref-to-string helper. (f) One cited line is slightly off: the render_errors block is lines 309-330 (finding says 313-329, close enough), and render_info is 271-290.
confirmedFindings.value_note: Split the fix into two risk tiers. Tier 1 (S, low risk, zero behavior change): delete the line-23 halt branch, drop `times` from the dispatch list, and remove the dead 'times' pop at Test2.pm:569 — verify first that Test2-Collector never emits a top-level `times` facet. Tier 2 (S, low-MEDIUM risk, user-visible output changes): using $msg in render_info/render_errors and un-shadowing $type in render_about changes rendered output — note these identical bugs exist verbatim in reference/legacy and reference/pre_ai_2.0 (canonical human code), i.e. they are inherited upstream bugs shipped on CPAN for years, so "restore evident intent" is actually a deliberate behavior change; check for renderer-output/snapshot tests before landing. Also: the two copies have already diverged (App::Yath2::Renderer::Default::Composer line 195 adds $_->{peek} to the info filter vs the Test2::Formatter copy) — apply fixes to BOTH files and either reconcile the divergence or have one delegate to the other to prevent future drift. Depends: none (independent of DB-Jsonl/#55/#56, #44, #61); could optionally be folded into any future default-renderer ticket, but none exists today.

confirmedFindings.title: Two competing gen_uuid implementations: Data::UUID (v1, uppercase) vs Test2::Util::UUID (v7, lowercase)
confirmedFindings.evidence: lib/Test2/Harness2/Util/UUID.pm: `use Data::UUID;` ... `sub gen_uuid { UG()->create_str() }` — Data::UUID mints v1-style UPPERCASE UUIDs. lib/App/Yath2/Util/UUID.pm: `my $T2_GEN_UUID = Test2::Util::UUID->get_gen_uuid->{gen_uuid}` ... `sub gen_uuid { return lc($T2_GEN_UUID->()) }` — v7 lowercase. STYLE_GUIDE.md 'UUIDs' section mandates: 'Use Test2::Util::UUID ... These are v7'. `grep -rln 'use Test2::Harness2::Util::UUID' lib | wc -l` = 12 importers (Plugin.pm, Renderer/Base.pm, JobReader.pm, RunnerReader.pm, Command/watch.pm, TestFile.pm, Role/Service/Connection.pm, Command/spawn.pm, Plugin/Cover.pm, Command/stop.pm, Options/Run.pm, Options/Runner.pm) vs 3 importers of the App::Yath2 one. Both export the same-named `gen_uuid` with different version AND case semantics.
confirmedFindings.proposal: Make Test2::Harness2::Util::UUID the single wrapper over Test2::Util::UUID (lowercased at generation, matching R9), have App::Yath2::Util::UUID reuse it for gen_uuid (keeping derive_uuid where it is), and drop the Data::UUID prereq from cpanfile/Makefile.PL. This removes the v1-vs-v7 and uppercase-vs-lowercase split before the DB logger (DB-4) starts persisting run/job UUIDs.
confirmedFindings.overlap: #48 / chunk DB-4 (R9 centralizes lowercasing in App::Yath2::Util::UUID, but does not retire the Data::UUID module the 12 Harness2-side call sites still use)
confirmedFindings.accuracy_note: Two corrections/softenings: (1) The uppercase-vs-lowercase half is partially mitigated by design — ARCHITECTURE.md (~lines 880-891, the finding's 888-890 cite is substantively right) states wire UUIDs are lowercased on ingest at the DB boundary (R9), so uppercase output will not persist as uppercase; the unmitigated substance is v1-vs-v7 (loses v7 time-ordering that STYLE_GUIDE relies on for index locality, and derive_uuid documents v7-base semantics). Correct fix: inside Test2::Harness2::Util::UUID replace Data::UUID with Test2::Util::UUID (output stays uppercase, so the 12 importers see only a v1→v7 version change, no case change), leave App::Yath2::Util::UUID as the lowercase boundary wrapper per #48, and drop the Data::UUID prereq from cpanfile/Makefile.PL. Effort M→S (one module + prereq removal; gen_uuid signature unchanged). Risk medium→low. Sequence before or with #48 in chunk DB-4 (must land before the DB logger persists run/job UUIDs, and before #57 which needs v7 timestamps). Depends: #48 (R9/derive), #57 (v7 timestamp assumption). Gotcha to note in the ticket: known Test2::Util::UUID load-order bug (see project memory project_quickorm_uuid_case).

confirmedFindings.title: cli_args defined in 28 commands is never called; help/POD machinery reads doc_args which nothing defines
confirmedFindings.evidence: Command.pm cli_help/generate_pod both use `my (@args) = $class->doc_args;` (Command.pm:60,109) with default `sub doc_args { () }` (Command.pm:20). No command overrides doc_args (grep -rn 'doc_args' lib/ t/ share/ release-scripts/ dist.ini hits only Command.pm). Meanwhile 28 command files define `sub cli_args { "..." }` (e.g. failed.pm:31 `sub cli_args { "[--] event_log.jsonl[.gz|.bz2] [job1, job2, ...]" }`) and grep -rn -- '->cli_args' lib/ t/ share/ release-scripts/ finds ZERO callers. Consequence is visible in shipped docs: failed.pm's release-generated POD USAGE reads `$ yath [YATH OPTIONS] failed [OPTIONS]` with no [COMMAND ARGUMENTS] section, even though the command requires a log-file argument.
confirmedFindings.proposal: Make the base default `sub doc_args { $_[0]->cli_args ? ($_[0]->cli_args) : () }` (or rename the 28 cli_args subs to doc_args) so the argument strings feed cli_help/generate_pod again; regenerate POD via release-scripts. Delete whichever name loses.
confirmedFindings.accuracy_note: Two refinements. (1) Historical context: the doc_args/cli_args split is inherited from the legacy 1.x tree (reference/legacy/lib/App/Yath/Command.pm has the identical doc_args-only base while its commands define cli_args), so this is carried-over dead code, not a 2.0d regression; however the canonical pre_ai_2.0 reference DID consume cli_args — reference/pre_ai_2.0/lib/App/Yath.pm:141-144 builds the usage line from $cmd_class->cli_args — so the fix could alternatively restore that consumer in App::Yath2's usage/help path. (2) 13 of the 28 cli_args definitions return "" (ps, reload, db, which, start, kill, watch, status, resources, recent, client/recent, list, db/sync, stop, abort, ping), so the proposal's truthiness guard (`cli_args ? (cli_args) : ()`) is required, and only ~15 commands would actually gain a COMMAND ARGUMENTS section.
confirmedFindings.value_note: Prefer the bridge over mass-rename: doc_args returns a LIST of strings or [name, description] pairs (Command.pm:80-96, 125-131), while every cli_args returns one usage-fragment string, so a blind rename yields one lumpy =item per command. Land base defaults `sub cli_args { '' }` and `sub doc_args { my $a = $_[0]->cli_args; length($a) ? ($a) : () }`, keep the 28 cli_args subs as-is, regenerate POD via release-scripts/generate_command_pod.pl, and add a test that commands with cli_args produce a [COMMAND ARGUMENTS] section in both cli_help and generate_pod. Sequencing note for a Depends line: chunk DB-1 (#45) will move/stub the db, server, and recent command files to reference/old_db — either land this first (the base-class bridge is unaffected) or after DB-1 to avoid regenerating POD for files about to be stubbed. Effort S and risk low stand; output is help text + generated POD only, no behavioral API.

confirmedFindings.title: stop.pm and kill.pm duplicate the runner-teardown tail; kill re-attaches the client the SUPER chain already attaches
confirmedFindings.evidence:
stop.pm:72-79 and kill.pm:46-49 are the same four-step tail: `sleep(0.02) while kill(0, $pid);` + `unlink($pfile...) if -f ...;` + `remove_tree($self->workdir, {safe => 1, keep_root => 0}) if -d $self->workdir;` + `print "

Runner stopped

" unless $self->settings->display->quiet;`. kill.pm additionally calls `$self->client->attach_runner($data->{pid})` (kill.pm:37) and then `$self->SUPER::run()` (abort.pm), whose first act is `$self->client->attach_runner($data->{pid})` again on the same cached client. kill.pm:46 also re-reads `$self->pfile_data->{pid}` when $data->{pid} is already in scope.
confirmedFindings.proposal: Add one helper on the persist family (e.g. `wait_and_cleanup_runner($pid)` in run.pm or stop.pm) used by both; drop kill.pm's redundant attach_runner and reuse $data->{pid}.
confirmedFindings.accuracy_note: The proposal's "drop kill.pm's redundant attach_runner" is wrong as stated and should be removed or reworded. kill.pm:37's attach cannot be dropped: it must run before kill's own $self->client->submitter->end_queue() at kill.pm:38, because the submitter is constructed with a liveness_check closure (Client.pm:679-687) that calls runner_gone(), which reports the runner as gone whenever RUNNER_PID is unset — the submitter would treat the runner as dead. The actually-duplicated attach is the one inside abort's SUPER::run (abort.pm:38), which also cannot be removed since abort is a standalone command. The double attach is a harmless idempotent two-field set (Client.pm:343-348), so this sub-claim is cosmetic, not actionable, without restructuring the call order. The pfile_data->{pid} re-read at kill.pm:46 is real but cosmetic (pfile is cached; banner prints once). The finding's real value is the shared wait_and_cleanup_runner($pid) helper for the two identical tails; effort S / risk low stands for that part.
confirmedFindings.value_note: Helper placement: run.pm is correct and is in fact the only shared ancestor — stop extends run directly, while kill extends abort extends status extends run — so `wait_and_cleanup_runner($pid, $pfile_path)` belongs in App::Yath2::Command::run (not stop.pm, which kill cannot see). Keep it taking the pfile path as an argument since the two callers derive it differently today. Note the SUPER-chain nuance when dropping kill.pm's attach_runner: kill's comment says it attaches early so end_queue can be sent BEFORE SUPER::run() (abort) does its truncate; the fix is to drop the SECOND attach only if refactoring abort, or simply leave abort's attach (it is the canonical one) and delete kill.pm:37's — either way verify end_queue still has an attached client before it fires. Add a Depends/related line for #51 (DB-4): it will make the runner defer its own workdir cleanup until subscribers disconnect, and the command-side remove_tree in this tail is the exact line that interacts with that — landing the shared helper first means #51 adjusts cleanup semantics in one place instead of two.

confirmedFindings.title: ps.pm declares an unused 'queue' HashBase slot and is the only persist sibling that never attaches the client to the runner pid
confirmedFindings.evidence: ps.pm:13 `use Test2::Harness2::Util::HashBase qw/queue/;` — grep -n 'queue' lib/App/Yath2/Command/ps.pm shows no other occurrence (no ->queue, no {+QUEUE}); the slot is a 1.0 leftover. Also, ps.pm run() does `my $data = $self->pfile_data(); ... my $status = $self->client->status // {};` (ps.pm:30-34) without the `$self->client->attach_runner($data->{pid})` step its parent status.pm (status.pm:36) and siblings abort/stop/watch/resources all perform — it works only because Client::submitter needs just the workdir, but the client's RUNNER_PID stays unset so its liveness fallback (runner_gone/kill(0)) cannot see the runner.
confirmedFindings.proposal: Drop the `queue` slot (plain `use Test2::Harness2::Util::HashBase;`) and add the same attach_runner($data->{pid}) call the parent uses (or hoist the pfile_data+attach pair into a run.pm helper all persist commands share).
confirmedFindings.accuracy_note: Overstatement to note: ps never consults runner_gone/liveness_check (single status query, no subscription), so the missing attach_runner has zero functional impact today — it is a consistency gap, not a latent bug in the current flow. Minor corrections: resources.pm is group 'state', not a 'persist' sibling (though it follows the same attach pattern); kill and ping also attach (finding listed only abort/stop/watch/resources); and the slot was unused even at its 1.0 introduction, so 'leftover' means copy-paste dead weight from day one rather than code that once worked. The proposal (drop the slot, add the attach call or hoist a shared pfile+attach helper) is safe: no external consumer of the generated queue accessor exists in lib/, t/, share/, release-scripts/, or dist.ini.
confirmedFindings.value_note: Keep effort S / risk low. Prefer the minimal fix: drop `qw/queue/` from the HashBase line and add `$self->client->attach_runner($data->{pid});` right after `my $data = $self->pfile_data();` in ps.pm::run(), mirroring status.pm:36. The proposal's 'hoist into a run.pm helper' variant is optional — run.pm already has the exact pair in start_runner (run.pm:238-245), but ps/status run() bodies are full overrides, so a hoist is only worthwhile if coordinated with the upcoming persist commands. Add: Depends: none; Related: #62 (REF-PORT list/ping — will add two more persist commands using the same discover+attach pattern; if the shared-helper variant is chosen, do it there), #41 (context: DONE client-library thinning that produced the current shape).

confirmedFindings.title: resources.pm re-runs Pfile discovery + client attach on every 0.2s poll and ignores the pfile/pfile_data helpers it inherits; unreachable return
confirmedFindings.evidence: resources.pm inherits status -> run, which provide cached `pfile`/`pfile_data` and the attach pattern every sibling uses, yet runner_resources (resources.pm:34-46) hand-rolls `App::Yath2::Pfile->find($self->settings, $self->pfile_params)` + `$pfile->data` + `kill(0,$pid)` + `$self->client->attach_runner($pid)`. run() then calls runner_resources inside `while (1) { ... sleep 0.2 }` (resources.pm:58), so the full symlink-walk discovery and attach repeat five times a second forever; the `return 0;` at resources.pm:78 after the infinite loop is unreachable (loop exits only via die/signal).
confirmedFindings.proposal: Do discovery once via the inherited `$self->pfile_data` + `$self->client->attach_runner(...)` before the loop and keep only `$self->client->resources` inside it; drop the unreachable return (or add a real exit condition like runner-gone, matching ping.pm).
confirmedFindings.accuracy_note: Two overstatements, neither fatal: (1) "ignores the pfile/pfile_data helpers" — the hand-rolled Pfile->find is not pure duplication for the INITIAL probe: the inherited pfile helper dies when no runner is found (run.pm:212-213), and resources.pm's `no_fatal => 1` pfile_params is silently deleted/ignored by Pfile::find (Pfile.pm:105), so runner_resources' undef-return semantics (needed for run()'s own die message and for tolerating a runner vanishing mid-loop) cannot be had from $self->pfile as-is. The real defect is repeating discovery INSIDE the loop, not the existence of a non-fatal probe. Any fix should keep non-fatal find semantics (or loosen the inherited helper), not blindly swap to $self->pfile_data which would change the error path. (2) "the attach pattern every sibling uses" — ping.pm also hand-rolls Pfile->find + attach_runner (once, pre-loop), so it is not literally every sibling; ping is the right model for the loop-exit condition, though. Minor: attach_runner itself is trivial (sets two hash fields, Client.pm:343-348), so the repeated attach is harmless noise; the material per-poll cost is the Discovery->find symlink-resolve + unix-socket connect probe. Cited line ranges are accurate.
confirmedFindings.value_note: Two adjustments to the proposal. (1) attach_runner is trivial (Client.pm:343 just records the pid, no socket work), so the per-poll cost claim should center on App::Yath2::Pfile->find (symlink walk + liveness connect) and $pfile->data, not the attach. (2) Naively switching to the inherited helpers changes behavior: run.pm's pfile() (run.pm:210-214) dies with "No persistent harness was found for the current path.\n" even with pfile_params' no_fatal (find returns undef -> `or die`), replacing resources.pm's softer "No persistent runner and no running test found\n" message, and pfile_data() (run.pm:216-225) prints a Found/PID/Dir discovery banner that the \e[2J screen-clear will wipe on the first repaint — either accept both or keep the custom die message wrapping the inherited call. Recommended shape: one-time discovery + attach before the loop (inherited pfile_data or the existing probe), loop body reduced to eval { $self->client->resources } with a runner-gone exit exactly like ping.pm's `if (!$reply) { ...; last }` (ping.pm:71-75), plus its SIGINT/SIGTERM flag pattern so Ctrl-C exits cleanly; drop the unreachable return or make it reachable via that exit path. Effort S and risk low stand. Depends: none pending; builds on completed #41 (chunk 30) client pattern; independent of #24/#59 (runner-side resource classes).

confirmedFindings.title: LiveProducer::asserts_seen has no callers and would always return 0 because the dispatch_cb redirect bypasses the engine's counter
confirmedFindings.evidence: grep -rn '->asserts_seen' lib t: the only producer-side caller is Command/replay.pm:82, which uses a JSONLFileProducer (has its own counter); Command/test.pm:442 and all t/AI RenderLoop tests call $loop->asserts_seen, which RenderLoop.pm:183 answers from the SINK (`sub asserts_seen ($self) { return $self->sink->asserts_seen }`), never the producer. Beyond being uncalled, the sub is wrong-by-construction: LiveProducer::init installs set_dispatch_cb on the engine, and Base::dispatch (Base.pm:527-533) short-circuits to the cb and returns before dispatch_to_sinks, where the ASSERTS_SEEN increment lives (Base.pm:562) — so the engine's count the sub delegates to stays 0 forever on the LiveProducer path.
confirmedFindings.proposal: Delete `sub asserts_seen` from LiveProducer (final_data/tests_seen stay: the engine genuinely owns those and RenderLoop delegates to them). If producer-side assert counts are ever needed, count in the queue callback instead.
confirmedFindings.accuracy_note: Cited lines are accurate. One addition to the proposal: also remove the POD advertising the method — LiveProducer.pm line 157 ("final_data / tests_seen / asserts_seen") and the "=item $n = $producer->asserts_seen" entry at lines 163-165 — otherwise the docs keep promising a producer-side assert tally that is always 0.
confirmedFindings.value_note: Extend the proposal slightly: besides deleting `sub asserts_seen` at LiveProducer.pm:175, remove its POD `=item $n = $producer->asserts_seen` block (lines ~163-175) and drop `asserts_seen` from the rollup-accessor list in the DESCRIPTION POD (~line 157), so the docs stop advertising it. Keep final_data/tests_seen: RenderLoop.pm:180-181 duck-types them off the producer via can(), and the engine genuinely owns them (their bookkeeping is not inside dispatch_to_sinks). confirmedFindings.title: Driver::_render_aborted rebuilds the launch event _render_launch already builds, under a comment claiming it is conditional

The comment at 359-360 says 'If the launch was never rendered (the collector never started), render it now' — but the dispatch at 384 is unconditional for every aborted job: the guard on line 362 (`return if $entry->{$job_id}++` on ABORTED_RENDERED, keyed by job_id) is independent of the `launched` flag _render_launch tracks in BY_UUID (keyed by collector uuid), so a job whose collector launched (launch already rendered) and was then watchdog-aborted gets a second synthetic launch line and a double tries/TESTS_SEEN increment.
confirmedFindings.proposal: Extract the launch-event construction+bookkeeping into a private `_dispatch_launch($job_id, $file, $try)` used by both, and make _render_aborted call it only when the job was never launched (track launched per job_id or consult BY_UUID via job lookup), matching the comment.
confirmedFindings.accuracy_note: Line-number corrections: _render_launch's bookkeeping is at 319-320 (not 313-314; 312 is the launched-flag guard), its event construction is 325-337 with dispatch at 339, and _render_aborted spans 348-419. confirmedFindings.value_note: Keep proposal, but the launched-tracking detail needs care: _render_launch keys `launched` in BY_UUID by collector uuid, and a retried job can have multiple collectors, so "consult BY_UUID" requires a collector→job reverse walk. confirmedFindings.title: Renderer::Formatter ignores half its constructor args and carries dead 'handles'/'output' plumbing; base Renderer's verbose/color accessors are write-only

confirmedFindings.title: Preload-root failure wind-down duplicated at four sites in Runner.pm; _handle_dead_preload_root's if/else branches are identical
confirmedFindings.evidence: Four copies of the same failure path `$self->_emit_preload_failure_output; $self->{+SIGNAL} //= 'TERM'`: run_scheduler_only's readiness loop at 1184-1188 (stage_host_exited), 1194-1198 (deadline), the mid-run check at 1249-1253, and _handle_dead_preload_root at 850-858 — where the if/else (846: `if ($self->stage_host_exited) { $self->_emit_preload_failure_output; } else { warn ...; $self->_emit_preload_failure_output; }`) differs only by one warn, and 1184-1188 duplicates the stage_host_exited handling _handle_dead_preload_root already performs on the very next line (1192). The documented ''/'fail' return contract (838-841) is consumed only as truthiness by both callers (1192, 1260).
confirmedFindings.proposal: Collapse to one helper, e.g. `_fail_preload($self, $warn_msg = undef)` that warns (if given), emits the captured errors, and sets SIGNAL//='TERM'; collapse _handle_dead_preload_root's if/else and return plain 1/0. Removes the duplicated stage_host_exited pre-check in the readiness loop.
confirmedFindings.accuracy_note: Three corrections: (1) Title overstates — the if/else branches are not "identical", they differ by the warn at line 854 (the evidence text already says this correctly). (2) The 1184-1188 readiness-loop pre-check is not a pure duplicate of 1192: stage_host_exited is set by a socket announcement (Runner/Role/Service/Handlers.pm:1127-1136) that arrives before the root process is reapable by _preload_root_dead's waitpid, so 1184 fails fast during the announced-but-not-yet-reaped window; removing it delays wind-down by a few 10ms ticks (or until the 1194 deadline in a hung-announcer edge case) — safe, but a minor behavior change, not zero-diff dedup. (3) Guard conditions differ per site (1249 additionally requires nonempty stage_host_errors), so extract only the action body (optional warn + emit + SIGNAL//='TERM'), keeping per-site guards. Also note t/AI/integration/Runner_scheduler_reap_a3.t:41 mocks _handle_dead_preload_root returning '' — keep the method name and falsy-when-alive contract (returning 1/0 is compatible).
confirmedFindings.value_note: Narrow the proposal: the safe extraction is the shared tail only — a `_fail_preload($warn_msg = undef)` that warns if given, calls _emit_preload_failure_output, and sets `$self->{+SIGNAL} //= 'TERM'` — plus collapsing _handle_dead_preload_root's cosmetically-different if/else (keep the two-scenario comment; fold the warn into the else-arm's `_fail_preload("...died unexpectedly...")` call) and returning plain 1/0 since both callers (Runner.pm:1192, 1260) use only truthiness. However, DROP the sub-proposal to "remove the duplicated stage_host_exited pre-check in the readiness loop": it is NOT redundant. _handle_dead_preload_root gates on _preload_root_dead (Runner.pm:819 — PRELOAD_ROOT_REAPED flag or a successful WNOHANG waitpid), while stage_host_exited is the socket announcement, which can be true before the root process is reaped; the pre-checks at 1184-1188 and 1249-1253 fire on the announcement without waiting for reap timing, and the mid-run site additionally has a deliberately different condition (`stage_host_exited && @{stage_host_errors}` — a clean announced exit at wind-down must NOT set SIGNAL). So: four call sites share one tail helper; do not merge the checks themselves. Also preserve the "must run AFTER _bring_out_yer_dead" ordering note (Runner.pm:1233-1238). Depends: none (all of #3/#4/#11/#18/#21 done); note in the ticket that chunk 16 (run-scoped preload stages) will later rework the readiness loop, so land this before chunk 16 starts.

confirmedFindings.title: Graceful-stop/reap poll loop copy-pasted three times across stop_preload_root and stop_sampler
confirmedFindings.evidence: stop_preload_root (989-995): `eval { $self->service_send('preload-root', 'stop'); 1 }; for (1 .. 250) { $self->service_io; last if waitpid($pid, POSIX::WNOHANG) == $pid; Time::HiRes::sleep(0.02); }`. stop_sampler repeats the identical send+loop at 1068-1074 (name 'sampler'), then repeats the loop a THIRD time at 1082-1086 (`for (1 .. 100)`) for the TERM escalation. Only the tails legitimately differ (preload-root must not be killed, 997-1008; sampler escalates TERM->KILL, 1080-1091).
confirmedFindings.proposal: Extract `_stop_and_reap_helper($self, $name, $pid, $tries)` (service_send 'stop' + the service_io/waitpid/sleep loop, returning whether the pid was reaped); both subs keep their distinct fallback tails. Removes two of the three loop copies.
confirmedFindings.accuracy_note: Minor: the third copy (1082-1086) is post-TERM and has no service_send, so the proposed helper that bundles service_send('stop') removes only two of three copies (as the finding itself states); making the send optional or extracting the bare poll loop (_reap_poll($pid, $tries)) would fold all three. Extraction should also preserve the distinct explanatory comments around each teardown (997-1008 preload-root orphaning rationale, 1076-1079 fd-closing rationale).
confirmedFindings.value_note: Refine the extraction shape: the truly identical unit repeated three times is the reap-poll loop, not the send+loop combo (the third copy at 1082-1086 has NO service_send - it follows kill('TERM') and uses 100 tries). So extract `_reap_poll($self, $pid, $tries)` (service_io + waitpid WNOHANG + Time::HiRes::sleep(0.02); returns true if reaped) and call it at all three sites; optionally a thin `_graceful_stop($self, $name, $pid, $tries)` wrapping the eval{service_send} + _reap_poll for the two graceful sites. Keep the distinct tails verbatim, including their load-bearing comments (preload-root must NOT be killed - ChildMonitor orphaning rationale at 997-1008; sampler TERM->KILL fd-closing rationale). Effort S and risk low are accurate; the eval should follow the house pattern `my $ok = eval { ...; 1 };` if touched. Depends: none (all related tickets #3/#4/#11/#27-#29 are closed); file as a new small TODO_TASKS ticket in the Runner-cleanup lineage. Verify with both canonical runners: AUTHOR_TESTING=1 prove -Ilib -j16 -r t/ and AUTHOR_TESTING=1 yath test -D -j16.

confirmedFindings.title: Shared runner hash keys accessed three different ways: HashBase constants, role-declared constants, and bare strings
confirmedFindings.evidence: Role::Scheduler declares constant-only slots precisely 'for compile-time/grep safety on the bare-string keys' (Scheduler.pm:8-11, the pattern TODO_TASKS #17 established), yet Runner.pm itself reads role-shared keys as bare strings: {'job_passed'} (1457), {'collector_reap'} (1525), {submit_buffer} (888, 901), {service_select} (541), {service_peers} (741, 762, 785, 1321), {service_subs} (567). Conversely Runner.pm declares `+monitor` (76) and `+job_pids` (82) as HashBase slots, but the Handlers role that owns those keys uses bare strings ({'monitor'} Handlers.pm:1148, {'job_pids'} Handlers.pm:349/869/976) — so the MONITOR constant is declared and never used by anyone, and a typo in any bare key would silently vivify a new slot.
confirmedFindings.proposal: Apply the #17 pattern uniformly: declare constant-only slots (in the role that owns them, as Role::Scheduler does) for job_passed/collector_reap/submit_buffer/monitor/job_pids and the service_* keys, and convert the bare-string accesses in Runner.pm and Handlers.pm to `{+CONST}`.
confirmedFindings.accuracy_note: Minor corrections: (1) service_peers line is 763, not 762. (2) JOB_PIDS is actually used in Runner.pm (lines 178, 1423), so job_pids is a genuine constant-vs-bare split (constant in Runner + StatusReport.pm, bare in Handlers); only MONITOR is declared-and-unused, as the finding states. (3) submit_buffer is not role-shared — both accesses (888, 901) are in Runner.pm itself; it merely lacks a declared slot. (4) The true owner of the service_* keys is lib/Test2/Harness2/Role/Service.pm, which itself uses bare strings for service_select/service_peers/service_subs at ~20 more sites (lines 198-475) and is also composed into Preload::Host, Sampler, etc. — a uniform fix must touch Role/Service.pm too, so the footprint is larger than the finding's file list (effort M still plausible, but scope note matters). (5) Additional uncited bare-string sites in Handlers.pm: 436 (job_passed write), 447/1332 (collector_reap), 1025 (service_peers).
confirmedFindings.value_note: Adjust effort M -> S: this is a mechanical sweep with an existing in-repo template (Role::Scheduler.pm:8-17). Two implementation notes for the proposal: (1) Role::Tiny role code compiles in the role's own package, so Runner.pm's +MONITOR/+JOB_PIDS constants are NOT visible inside Handlers.pm — Handlers must declare its own constant-only HashBase slots (same comment/pattern as Role::Scheduler), and each role should declare the keys it owns (job_passed/collector_reap likely belong to the completion/handler role, service_* to the service role) with Runner.pm consuming them via {+CONST}. (2) Verify slot ownership before moving: the finding says Runner declares +monitor/+job_pids but Handlers owns the accesses — keep the declaration in Runner (it constructs the hash) and add matching constant-only declarations in Handlers, per the "owning runner declares the same slots; the values match" convention already documented in Scheduler.pm:11-12. Suggested Depends line: extends #17 (DONE, pattern source); coordinate lightly with pending chunks 22/23 only if they land first and rename run-state-adjacent keys (none of the listed keys are expected casualties). Consider adding a one-line author-test grep forbidding new bare-string self-hash keys in Runner*/Role* to keep the invariant from regressing.

confirmedFindings.title: Two HashBase sources in the same directory, and the direct Object::HashBase dependency is not declared in dist.ini
confirmedFindings.evidence: StatusReport.pm:8 `use Object::HashBase` (as do 10 other shipped Runner/* modules: Watchdog, Monitor, Resource*, ...), while Runner.pm:35, State.pm:20, Run.pm:11 and Role/Scheduler.pm:12 use the bundled generated copy `Test2::Harness2::Util::HashBase` ('This is a generated file!' header; bundling exists so the dist does not depend on the Object-HashBase CPAN dist). dist.ini's manual [Prereqs] block (lines 63-146, no AutoPrereqs plugin) does not list Object::HashBase, so every direct `use Object::HashBase` in shipped code is an undeclared runtime dependency — a clean install without Object-HashBase fails to load StatusReport et al.
confirmedFindings.proposal: Pick one source: either add Object::HashBase to [Prereqs] and (per STYLE_GUIDE 'Use Object::HashBase') migrate the legacy modules over time, or switch the 11 direct users to the bundled Test2::Harness2::Util::HashBase (mechanical, same API). Either way the undeclared-dep hole closes.
confirmedFindings.accuracy_note: The stated failure scenario is wrong and overstates severity: dist.ini:81 declares Test2::Collector = 0.000002 as a hard runtime prereq, and Test2-Collector itself declares Object::HashBase = 0.016 (Test2-Collector dist.ini:53/cpanfile:15/Makefile.PL), so a clean install always gets Object::HashBase transitively — StatusReport et al. do NOT fail to load. The real issue is dependency hygiene (shipped code directly using a module only guaranteed via a transitive dep) plus the two-HashBase-sources inconsistency. Also a count fix: 10 files use Object::HashBase directly, not 11 (finding says StatusReport + 10 others); Resource.pm's second occurrence at line 147 is inside POD example text. Proposal remains valid; note that if migrating direct users to the bundled copy, the STYLE_GUIDE/STYLE_GUIDE_AGENT_CHECKLIST wording ('Use Object::HashBase') should be clarified to name the bundled module.
confirmedFindings.value_note: Correct the proposal's "mechanical, same API" claim: the bundled Test2::Harness2::Util::HashBase is generated from Object::HashBase 0.008 (header says HB_VERSION 0.008; its import has no `&Role` handling), while three direct users — lib/Test2/Harness2/Runner/Resource.pm, Resource/JobCount.pm, Resource/Preload.pm — rely on the 0.019 `&Role` Role::Tiny-composition syntax deliberately introduced by DONE ticket #24. Pointing them at the bundled 0.008 copy would silently mis-parse `&Test2::...` as an attribute name and break role composition. Revised proposal: (1) cheapest immediate fix — add Object::HashBase (>= 0.019) to dist.ini [Prereqs], closing the undeclared-dep hole; or (2) regenerate the bundled copy from Object::HashBase 0.019 via hashbase_inc.pl, then mechanically switch the 10 direct-user files to it. Either way, resolve the doc conflict: ARCHITECTURE §2.1 and STYLE_GUIDE say "use Object::HashBase" while pending ticket #61 (REF-PORT) instructs swapping Object::HashBase → the bundled Util::HashBase (the 99-file majority convention) — update whichever docs lose. Effort: S for option 1; S-M for option 2 (regeneration + verify `&Role` works in the regenerated bundle). Risk stays low. Depends: relates to #24 (DONE — origin of the &Role usage), #61 (pending — prescribes bundled copy for new code), #58/#59 (pending — extend Disk/UnixLimits, two of the affected files).

"<kind>-$$"` lazy default, and `sub CONNECT_TIMEOUT { 30 }` (Client.pm:198 / Subscriber.pm:198). The only real difference is Client's liveness_check/runner_gone escape inside the loop; both classes' reply-wait loops (Client::_request 259-271, Subscriber::subscribe 141-164) also share the drain/croak-closed/croak-timeout/sleep-0.01 shape.
confirmedFindings.proposal: Extract a shared Role::Tiny role (e.g. Test2::Harness2::Runner::Role::SocketClient) providing socket_path, identity(kind), CONNECT_TIMEOUT, and a _connect that takes an optional liveness-check hook; compose it into both classes. confirmedFindings.title: Job::switches() runs three near-identical dedup loops with the -w detection line copy-pasted three times

The same `m/\s*-w\s*/` pattern appears a fourth time, negated, in use_fork at line 567.
confirmedFindings.proposal: Collapse to one loop over the three source lists with a single %seen hash (preserving cross-source precedence; decide intra-source dup behavior explicitly), and hoist the -w regex into one predicate/constant shared with use_fork.
confirmedFindings.accuracy_note: Two small additions: (1) any consolidation must preserve the current semantics exactly — dedup across sources but not within a source — since precedence is task > runner > env and the naive single `next if $seen{$s}++` would silently change intra-source behavior (the finding already hints at this); (2) the regex itself is loose (`\s*` is zero-width, so it matches any switch merely containing "-w", e.g. "-wfoo"), which is a further argument for hoisting it into one named predicate shared with use_fork so any future fix lands in one place.
confirmedFindings.value_note: Verified at lib/Test2/Harness2/Runner/Job.pm:615-644 and 566. Adjust the proposal: (1) preserve the intra-source-duplicates-kept asymmetry exactly (one helper loop over the three source lists, checking only prior sources' seen-set) rather than "deciding dup behavior explicitly" — changing it silently alters emitted switches; make any dup-policy change a separate follow-up with a test. (2) Hoist m/\s*-w\s*/ into a single shared predicate (e.g. _is_w_switch) used by both switches() and use_fork(), but do NOT tighten the regex in this pass (it currently matches '-w' as a substring; \s* is zero-width). confirmedFindings.title: Runner::Preload DEFAULT_STAGE holds a stage NAME or a StageConfig OBJECT depending on whether the preload declared a default; all consumers require a name
confirmedFindings.evidence: Preload.pm:180-184 `sub default_stage { return $self->{+DEFAULT_STAGE} if ...; return $self->{+STAGE_LIST}->[0]; }` — STAGE_LIST holds StageConfig objects, while set_default_stage (via the `default` DSL export) stores a name string; merge (line 177) `$self->{+DEFAULT_STAGE} //= $merge->default_stage;` caches the object permanently when the preload module never called `default()`. Consumers treat it as a name: Host.pm:257 `default => (defined($default) && $name eq $default) ? 1 : 0` (an object stringifies to StageConfig=HASH(...) and never matches, so no stage is flagged default in the stage map) and Preloader.pm:108 `return $self->{+STAGED}->default_stage;` returns it as the task's stage name. Grep `default_stage` across lib/ confirms these are the only consumers.
confirmedFindings.proposal: Make default_stage always return a name: `return $self->{+STAGE_LIST}->[0] ? $self->{+STAGE_LIST}->[0]->name : undef;` so DEFAULT_STAGE/consumers see one type.
confirmedFindings.overlap: chunk 23 (client-side stage assignment, #10/#20/#21) touches this resolution path but does not track this name-vs-object defect.
confirmedFindings.accuracy_note: Overstated slightly in impact, not in fact: on the primary path (preload-root hosts stages), the Host.pm defect is masked by State::_default_stage_from_map (State.pm:886-896), which defensively falls back to the alphabetically-first stage when none is flagged default — so the symptom is silent wrong-default selection (alphabetically-first stage instead of first-declared stage), not a crash or missing default handling. The harder failure (StageConfig object used as a stage/bucket key) only occurs via Preloader.pm:108, which requires an in-runner staged preloader (State.pm:849 branch), a secondary/no-preload-root configuration. Proposal is sound; note the merge line 177 should also stop caching objects (e.g. cache $merge->default_stage only when the merged meta's DEFAULT_STAGE name is set, or normalize to ->name there too).
confirmedFindings.value_note: Adjust proposal to fix both spots: (1) default_stage fallback returns $self->{+STAGE_LIST}[0] ? $self->{+STAGE_LIST}[0]->name : undef; (2) the merge cache at Preload.pm:177 ($self->{+DEFAULT_STAGE} //= $merge->default_stage) can permanently cache the fallback — either have merge copy only an explicitly-set DEFAULT_STAGE (preferred; keeps later-added stages able to shift the implicit default) or normalize in default_stage with blessed($v) ? $v->name : $v. Add a test: multi-stage preload without default() yields a Host stage map with exactly one default=>1 (first-declared stage) and Preloader::task_stage returns a plain name. Rewrite the overlap note: chunk 23/#10/#11 are DONE, so nothing pending to fold into; Depends: none (relates to landed #10/#23, ARCHITECTURE §4.7a stage-map resolution). confirmedFindings.title: Reloader's stat-poll throttle never engages: STAT_LAST_CHECKED is never stored (dead store to a lexical), making stat_min_gap inert and the comment wrong
confirmedFindings.evidence: Reloader.pm:153-158: `# Do not hammer the disk getting stat` ... `my $last_checked = $self->{+STAT_LAST_CHECKED}; return if $last_checked && $gap && ...; $last_checked = $check_time;` — the final assignment writes the lexical, not `$self->{+STAT_LAST_CHECKED}`. Grep for STAT_LAST_CHECKED across lib/ shows only the attr declaration (36), a delete in reset (74), and the read (156) — no write ever. So the guard at 157 is always false, the `stat_min_gap => 2` Preloader passes (Preloader.pm:75) and the `<stat_min_gap` attribute do nothing.
confirmedFindings.proposal: Store it on the object: `$self->{+STAT_LAST_CHECKED} = $check_time;` (or delete the whole throttle plus the stat_min_gap attribute/constructor arg if the caller-side 1s gate in Preloader::check is deemed sufficient — but then remove the misleading comment too).
confirmedFindings.accuracy_note: Two clarifications: (1) The dead store is inherited verbatim from the legacy 1.x code (reference/legacy/lib/Test2/Harness/Runner/Reloader.pm:157-159 has the same bug), so this is a faithfully ported pre-existing defect, not a port regression — and fixing it by writing $self->{+STAT_LAST_CHECKED} = $check_time would ENABLE a 2-second throttle that has never actually been in effect, increasing worst-case reload-detection latency on the non-inotify stat path from ~1s (Preloader's LAST_UPDATE gate) to ~2s; that behavior change should be a deliberate choice. (2) Impact scope is limited: the affected code path only runs when USE_INOTIFY is false (non-Linux platforms or missing Linux::Inotify2), and Preloader::check's 1s gate already caps stat frequency, so this is a code-hygiene/misleading-comment issue more than a disk-hammering one. The delete-the-throttle option in the proposal is arguably the safer fix.
confirmedFindings.value_note: Downgrade the implied severity: there is no disk-hammering bug in practice. Preloader::check (lib/Test2/Harness2/Runner/Preloader.pm:645-647, LAST_UPDATE) already throttles the entire check to once per second, and the stat path only executes on non-inotify platforms (Linux uses inotify). So this is dead-code/misleading-comment cleanup, not a performance fix. Prefer the deletion variant of the proposal: remove the broken throttle block (Reloader.pm:153-158), the STAT_LAST_CHECKED/STAT_MIN_GAP attrs (lines 36, 58, 74) and the stat_min_gap constructor arg (Preloader.pm:75), since the caller-side 1s gate is the real and sufficient throttle — note that fixing the store instead would change behavior (stat fallback drops from ~1s to ~2s cadence on non-Linux), which deletion avoids. Effort S, risk low, single consumer (Preloader is the only Reloader user). Depends: none. Related: TODO_TASKS #7 (misc fossils — file as a new 7-style sub-item; 7a precedent for Reloader.pm cleanup).

confirmedFindings.title: Hand-written new() + 'sub new;' predeclare in all six resource classes duplicates what HashBase already generates
confirmedFindings.evidence: Each of the six resource classes carries the same three-line block: `# Predeclare new() so HashBase does not generate one (we define our own below).` / `sub new;` plus `sub new { my $class = shift; my $self = bless {@_}, $class; $self->init(); return $self; }`. Object::HashBase's generated new is a strict superset of this (bless {@_} then call init when defined, plus hashref-arg support). Verified empirically: a class composing `&Test2::Harness2::Runner::Resource` via `use Object::HashBase qw{&... <attrs}` with no custom new gets a working generated new that blesses key/value args and calls init (test run: constructed object, init fired, defaults applied). All construction sites (State.pm:91, State.pm:101, State.pm:114) pass key/value pairs, the only form the hand-written new supports anyway.
confirmedFindings.proposal: Delete the `sub new;` predeclaration, the comment, and the custom `sub new` from all six classes and let Object::HashBase generate the constructor. Behavior is unchanged (init is still called); ~40 lines of ritual boilerplate and a misleading comment disappear from every resource file, and future resource classes stop cargo-culting it.
confirmedFindings.accuracy_note: One mechanism clarification for the implementer (does not change the verdict): the `sub new;` predeclare is load-bearing *as long as the custom new exists*. HashBase decides whether to generate new at `use Object::HashBase` compile time via `$into->can('new')` (HashBase.pm:110); the forward declaration `sub new;` makes `can('new')` truthy so HashBase skips generation, avoiding a "Subroutine new redefined" warning when the later `sub new {...}` body is compiled. So the predeclare must NOT be deleted in isolation — but the finding correctly removes the predeclare, comment, AND custom new together, after which HashBase generates new with no warning and identical behavior. The proposal is sound as written. Line numbers and file citations all verified exact.
confirmedFindings.value_note: Strengthen the evidence line: the base Resource.pm POD (lines 138-140, 386) already asserts HashBase provides new() to the composing class, so the hand-written new() and its "Predeclare new() so HashBase does not generate one" comment are not just redundant but actively contradict the documented base-class contract — removing them realigns the code with its own spec. confirmedFindings.title: run_cmd error-path die closures are triplicated and dereference optional caller1/caller2 params that only one caller supplies
confirmedFindings.evidence: Util/IPC.pm builds three near-identical error-formatter closures: swap_io's default (lines 55-59: `die("$_[0] at $caller[1] line $caller[2] ($caller2[1] ...")`), _run_cmd_fork's $die (133-140: `my $msg = "$_[0] at $caller1->[1] line $caller1->[2] ($caller2->[1] line $caller2->[2]).\n"; ... POSIX::_exit(127)`), and _run_cmd_spwn's $die (177-184, same plus a __FILE__/__LINE__ suffix). The fork/spwn variants dereference $params{caller1}/$params{caller2} with no defined-check. Grep `grep -rn "caller1\|caller2" lib t` shows the ONLY caller passing them is Test2::Harness2::IPC::spawn (IPC.pm:292); direct run_cmd callers App/Yath2/Client.pm:321, App/Yath2/Tester.pm:186, App/Yath2/Plugin/Git.pm:33, App/Yath2/Command/test.pm:271 pass neither.
confirmedFindings.proposal: Compute caller info inside run_cmd itself (e.g. `$params{caller1} //= [caller(0)]; $params{caller2} //= [caller(1) ? caller(1) : caller(0)]`), extract one shared die-formatter helper used by both backends (and as swap_io's default), and drop the caller1/caller2 forwarding from IPC::spawn.
confirmedFindings.accuracy_note:
Three corrections/additions, none of which undermine the finding (they strengthen or slightly de-escalate it):

1. The pattern is QUADRUPLICATED, not just triplicated. A fourth near-identical die closure lives in lib/Test2/Harness2/Runner/JobLauncher.pm:538-545 (print to cloned STDERR + STDERR, then POSIX::_exit(127)), differing only in that it computes caller live (like swap_io's default) instead of reading params. Any shared die-formatter helper should absorb this one too.

2. The undef deref is cosmetic/latent, not a crash. Under `use strict`, an rvalue `$caller1->[1]` on an undef scalar returns undef (no autovivification of the top scalar, no fatal error) — it only emits "uninitialized value" warnings inside the already-fatal error message. It also only fires on error paths (swap_io failure / exec failure) of direct run_cmd callers. So the practical impact is a garbled error line, not a functional bug. The category "spaghetti"/maintainability is the right framing; there is no correctness regression in the happy path.

3. swap_io's default die (55-59) is not exercised by any current in-repo caller: _swap_in_io always forwards a $die, and JobLauncher passes its own. It remains a legitimate defensive default for the exported swap_io() API, so it is not dead code — but the "shared as swap_io's default" part of the proposal touches a currently-unexercised branch.
confirmedFindings.value_note: Narrow the proposal: the IO-swap extraction the original 'proposal' implies is already done (_swap_in_io exists via #25), so scope this to (1) defaulting $params{caller1}//=[caller...] / caller2 inside run_cmd so the $die path never derefs undef for the 4 direct callers, and (2) collapsing the two backend $die closures + swap_io's default into one shared formatter. Preserve the deliberate message difference: swap_io's default and _run_cmd_spwn append a '${\__FILE__} line ${\__LINE__}' suffix while _run_cmd_fork does not — unify intentionally rather than by accident. Effort is closer to S than M given _swap_in_io already exists. Risk low. Depends/relates: #25 (DONE, extracted _swap_in_io), #8/chunk 21 (Util::IPC kept as primitive) — reference these on the Depends line. Only consumer of caller1/caller2 forwarding is Test2::Harness2::IPC::spawn (IPC.pm:285-292), so dropping the forwarding is safe.

confirmedFindings.title: Role::Service has three copy-paste teardown methods (close_service / reset_service / close_all_connections) with inconsistent close semantics
confirmedFindings.evidence: All three methods repeat the same block: iterate/close handles, then `delete $self->{service_listen}; delete $self->{service_select}; $self->{service_conns} = {}; $self->{service_peers} = {}; $self->{service_subs} = {};` (lines 438-442, 454-458, 473-475). reset_service (447-461) and close_service (463-483) share an identical select-handle close loop verbatim. They also disagree on how connections are closed: close_service calls `$_->close for values %$conns` (464-466) AND then re-closes the same fhs via the select loop (468-471, a double close), while reset_service closes raw fhs only, never marking the Connection objects closed.
confirmedFindings.proposal: Extract one private `_teardown_service(%opts)` (flags: unlink_path, reset_stopped, conn_objects_vs_raw_close) and make the three public methods thin documented calls into it; pick one connection-close style (Connection->close) so objects are consistently marked closed.
confirmedFindings.accuracy_note:
Keep refuted=false, but the finding overstates the "copy-paste inconsistency" and one evidence detail is wrong:

1. The three methods handle genuinely different, DOCUMENTED cases (POD at lines 114-133): close_service = shutdown + unlink socket path; close_all_connections = post-fork close-sweep in a no-exec child that must NOT unlink (parent owns the path) and uses CORE::close on the listen socket rather than the select loop; reset_service = reset-for-rebind and additionally sets `service_stopped=0` (line 459). So the differing close semantics are intentional and documented, not accidental drift. A refactor is fine but should preserve these deliberate differences.

2. The evidence's prose ("then delete service_listen; delete service_select; ...") is not uniformly true. Only close_all_connections (438-439) and reset_service (454-455) do `delete service_listen; delete service_select`. close_service does NEITHER as written: it deletes service_listen only conditionally inside the unlink guard (line 477) and never deletes service_select at all — it leaves `$self->{service_select}` pointing at a now-empty IO::Select. So the three "reset blocks" are not verbatim-identical; the genuinely-shared code is the 3-line conns/peers/subs clear (all three) plus the select-close loop (two of three).

3. The "double close" in close_service is real but harmless (second CORE::close just returns false); it's a cleanliness nit, not a bug.

Net: this is a legitimate but low-value S/low-risk maintainability cleanup (a small shared state-clear + one duplicated loop), not the pervasive "three copy-paste methods" the title implies.

confirmedFindings.accuracy_note: Two small line-range/scope corrections (do not change the verdict): (1) The drain ladder's real sysread block is 268-282 (266-267 are just `$fh`/`$buf` setup), and Control's _fill ladder ends at 243, not 246 (244-246 append to BUFFER and return the byte count). confirmedFindings.title: File::JSON::maybe_read re-implements parent maybe_read+read instead of adding just the empty-file guard
confirmedFindings.evidence: JSON.pm's maybe_read copies the parent's `-e` check, the Util::read_file call, and the `eval { $out = $self->decode($out); 1 } or confess "$self->{+NAME}: $@"` decode/error line from File.pm::read verbatim, adding only `return undef unless defined($out) && length($out)`. If File::read's decode error context or read path ever changes (e.g. richer confess message), maybe_read on JSON files silently keeps the old behavior while read gets the new one.
confirmedFindings.proposal: Reduce the override to the guard plus delegation: `return undef unless -e $self->{+NAME} && -s _; return $self->SUPER::maybe_read();` (an empty file is the only case the extra length-check catches).
confirmedFindings.accuracy_note: Two small notes: (1) the proposed `-s _` guard checks on-disk size before reading whereas the current code checks `length($out)` after read_file — equivalent for the empty-file case but slightly different semantics; (2) SUPER::maybe_read will redundantly re-run the `-e` check, which is harmless. Neither undermines the finding.
confirmedFindings.value_note: Keep the finding. The proposed patch is sound: `return undef unless -e $self->{+NAME} && -s _; return $self->SUPER::maybe_read();`. The `-s _` reuses the stat buffer and correctly maps an empty file to undef (matching the original `length($out)` guard); whitespace-only files still decode as before. Only nit: SUPER::maybe_read re-stats -e (one trivial redundant stat) — acceptable. No Depends line needed; this area is not tied to the DB chunks or any open ticket.

confirmedFindings.title: ByTest::finalize pushes wrapper-shaped records that no consumer can read (shape differs from stop_test)
confirmedFindings.evidence: stop_test (ByTest.pm:33) pushes the bare in-progress value onto COMPLETED: 'push @{$self->{+COMPLETED}} => delete $self->{+IN_PROGRESS}->{$test};' — a hashref shaped {test => ..., files => {...}, aggregator => ...}. finalize (ByTest.pm:91) instead pushes a wrapper keyed by test name: 'push @{$cm} => {$_ => delete $ip->{$_}} for keys %$ip;' — shaped { 't/foo.t' => {test..., files...} }. Every consumer expects the stop_test shape: lib/App/Yath2/Plugin/Cover.pm:216 reads '$list->[0]->{manager}, files => $list->[0]->{files}, test => $list->[0]->{test}', and the jsonl encode (Cover.pm:198, 'sub { encode_json($_[0]) . "\n" }') writes whatever shape is flushed, so a coverage .jsonl line emitted at finalize has a different schema from all other lines.
confirmedFindings.proposal: Change ByTest.pm:91 to push the bare value: 'push @$cm => delete $ip->{$_} for keys %$ip;' so finalize-flushed (never-ended, e.g. bail-out) tests have the same record shape as normally-completed tests. Add a regression test that finalizes with a test still in progress.

IN_PROGRESS is only non-empty at finalize when a test started but never got harness_job_end (bail-out/crash/abnormal termination). In normal runs COMPLETED is drained per-job and finalize writes nothing extra (hence coverage2.t passes clean). Keep effort S. No related tickets exist, so no Depends line (overlap correctly null). The regression test should drive a job-start-without-job-end through the aggregator and assert finalize->[0]{files} and {test} are populated in the bare shape.

confirmedFindings.title: Captured $err is never used; warn interpolates $@ instead, violating the repo's own eval-error rule
confirmedFindings.evidence:
Both files do 'my $ok = eval { ... 1; }; my $err = $@;' then execute another statement ('next if $ok;' at ByRun.pm:163 / 'return @out if $ok;' at ByTest.pm:164) before the failure path warns with the raw '$@': ByRun.pm:165 and ByTest.pm:166 both say 'warn "Error processing coverage data for '$test' using manager '$manager'...Error:
====
$@
====
";'. $err is assigned and never read (grep: 'grep -n "\$err" ByRun.pm ByTest.pm' shows only the assignment lines). STYLE_GUIDE.md's eval section requires later code to use the saved local precisely because intervening statements can clobber $@.
confirmedFindings.proposal: Use the captured variable in the warn ($err instead of $@) in both files; this is a two-character-class fix per file and makes the three-step eval pattern consistent with the rest of the codebase.
confirmedFindings.accuracy_note: Two clarifications, neither changes the verdict: (1) This is a style-guide/consistency defect, not a live functional bug. The only statements between the eval close-brace and the warn are `next if $ok;` (ByRun) / `return @out if $ok;` (ByTest); evaluating the scalar `$ok` and executing next/return cannot clobber `$@`, so `$@` currently still holds the correct error at the warn. The value of the fix is exactly what the style guide argues: robustness against future edits inserting a $@-clobbering statement, plus eliminating the dead `$err`. The finding already frames it this way ("violating the repo's own eval-error rule", "$err is assigned and never read"), so no overstatement. (2) The proposal's "two-character-class fix" is accurate — swap `$@` for `$err` in the warn string in each file.

confirmedFindings.title: manager_data merge logic duplicated between ByRun::touch and ByTest::touch (plus a dead $files assignment)
confirmedFindings.evidence: Both touch() implementations unpack the identical four params (source/sub/test/manager_data) and then run the same mdata merge: 'return unless $mdata; my $type = ref $mdata; if ($type eq \'ARRAY\') { my %seen; @$set = grep { !$seen{$_}++ } @$set, @$mdata; } else { push @$set => $mdata; }' (ByRun.pm:50-59 vs ByTest.pm:56-70 — ByTest only adds an '@$set empty' fast path). Only the $set lookup differs (ByRun.pm:48 keys by file/sub/test into the run-wide hash; ByTest.pm:54 keys by test/file/sub into in_progress). Relatedly, ByRun::record_coverage assigns 'my $files = $coverage->{files} //= {};' at ByRun.pm:23 and never uses $files in that sub (grep '$files' in ByRun.pm: only lines 23 and 46 use it; line 23's is write-only apart from the //= side effect).
confirmedFindings.proposal: Add a base-class helper, e.g. sub _merge_manager_data($self, $set, $mdata), and have both touch() methods reduce to their one-line $set lookup plus the helper call. Delete the unused 'my $files = ...' in ByRun::record_coverage (keep '$coverage->{files} //= {};' as a bare statement if the key-guarantee side effect is wanted, with a comment).
confirmedFindings.accuracy_note: One nuance a fix must respect: ByTest's empty-set fast path (`push @$set => @$mdata`) does NOT dedup internal duplicates within @$mdata, whereas ByRun's grep-based merge always dedups. This is a tiny behavioral divergence, so extracting a shared helper should keep the dedup path (which produces the same result for a genuinely empty set) rather than blindly copying either branch. Also note the //= side effect on ByRun.pm:23 is itself redundant (touch() already guarantees the `files` key), so it can be dropped entirely rather than kept as a bare statement — the "keep bare statement" option in the proposal is optional, not needed.
confirmedFindings.value_note: Accurate but tighten the risk note: the two touch() bodies are NOT byte-identical — ByRun always uses the grep-dedup form, while ByTest has an extra empty-$set fast path (`push @$set => @$mdata`, a flatten with no dedup) that only runs when $set is empty. The extracted `_merge_manager_data` helper should standardize on the grep-dedup form, which is behavior-equivalent to ByTest's fast path (dedup over an empty set is a no-op), so the refactor is safe but the reviewer/implementer must verify the flatten-vs-dedup equivalence rather than assume the bodies were literally the same. Also confirm no other subclass overrides touch() before promoting the helper to the base class (Test2::Harness2::Log::CoverageAggregator). The dead `my $files = ...` deletion in ByRun::record_coverage is independent and trivially safe. confirmedFindings.title: TestFile::queue_item duplicates the full ~24-field task shape in its directive-error branch

Add a soft 'Depends/Related: #58' line since #58 rewrites the same queue path (parser side) and touches E1 — sequence this cleanup alongside or just after #58 to avoid a rebase collision, and #58's E1 test additions can double as regression coverage that the error-task shape stays complete. confirmedFindings.title: Discovery::resolves reimplements the live-probe half of Discovery::probe

This is harmless (pid caches into $self->{+PID}, and the value is only ever beneficial to the returned instance), but it is a minor behavior change, not a pure no-op, so the "low risk" rating is fair but the reviewer should note the added filesystem touch. (2) Line ranges are exact: resolves is 275-285, probe is 314-347.

confirmedFindings.title: Insertion-ordered '@'-key map maintenance is copy-pasted at six sites that cross-reference each other by comment
confirmedFindings.evidence: The same idiom — vivify a Map hashref, then `push @{$ref->{'@'}} => $key unless exists $ref->{$key}` to keep an insertion-ordered class list — is hand-rolled in Display's renderers trigger (328-343), Run's load_import trigger (386-401), Run's dbi_profiling post (487-493), Runner's cover_post_process (677-684, comment: 'same pattern as Run.pm's dbi_profiling post and the load_import trigger'), Cover's post_process (152-159, comment: 'per Run.pm dbi_profiling pattern'), and Logging's inject_jsonl_renderer (197-211, 'the same shape Options/Display builds'). Each copy re-derives the subtle invariants (trigger fires before the key is stored so `exists` is false on first insert; walking flat pair lists for the JSON-hashref case), and Cover's copy needed an extra check_option guard the others lack — divergence has already started.
confirmedFindings.proposal: Extract one helper (e.g. Test2::Harness2::Util::ordered_map_insert($href, $key, $val) plus a vivify variant for the settings-post case) and replace the six bodies; the comments then shrink to one explanation at the helper.
confirmedFindings.accuracy_note:
Two corrections, both leaving the finding intact (and mostly strengthening it):

1. The finding UNDERCOUNTS the duplication. There is at least a seventh instance of the same idiom the finder missed: Display.pm:423-426 (the default-renderer post-process), which does `return if $renderers->{'@'} && @{...}; push @{$renderers->{'@'}} => 'Test2::Harness2::Renderer::Formatter'; $renderers->{...} = \@args;` — i.e. the same "append to '@' insertion-order list + store class-keyed args" maintenance. Display.pm:398 also mutates the same '@' list (grep-filter to drop the Formatter class). So the pattern is even more pervasive than the six sites cited.

2. The proposal's "one helper (plus a vivify variant)" is slightly optimistic. There are genuinely three shapes, not two: (a) the trigger sites walk a flat pair list and must NOT store the class-keyed value (the option framework stores it after the trigger returns) — idempotency via `exists`; (b) the settings-post sites vivify via create_option and DO store the value explicitly — idempotency via truthiness of `$h->{$key}`; (c) Logging uses grep-based idempotency and `//=`. A single `ordered_map_insert($href,$key,$val)` cleanly covers (b) and (c), but the trigger case needs a value-less variant (or a flag) since writing `$href->{$key}=$val` there would be wrong. This doesn't undermine the finding — it just means the consolidation is ~2-3 small helpers, not literally one; the core '@'-sync invariant is still the shared, duplicated piece worth extracting. Line ranges are all accurate.

confirmedFindings.accuracy_note: Two small line-number corrections (do not affect the conclusion): (a) The duplicated autofill block in DB/ORM.pm is at lines 60-65 (inside the `connection` sub whose signature is line 52), not spanning 52-67 as cited. (b) Reinforce the evidence: `require` (not `use`) never runs import(), and even Schema.pm's own `use DBIx::QuickORM` installs qorm() into App::Yath2::Schema's namespace — never the caller's — so the inline comment is wrong on two counts, strengthening the "no-op" claim. Empirical proof (built a live connection with Schema.pm never loaded, row class still generated as App::Yath2::Schema::Row::Hosts) is the decisive datum; the finder's static analysis matches runtime behavior exactly. The proposal (delete Schema.pm + the 7 requires, or reduce Schema.pm to a one-line delegator) is sound; note the requires also redundantly pull in DBIx::QuickORM, which DB/ORM.pm already loads, so removing them loses nothing.

confirmedFindings.title: client/recent.pm: --max/$count is computed and forwarded but never used (dead option), and get_data is a pass-through wrapper adding a third redundant error path
confirmedFindings.evidence: run() computes `my $count = $recent->max || 10;` (line 56) and calls `$self->get_data($project, $count, $user) or die "Could not get any data.\n"` (line 59). get_data (lines 102-107) is `return $self->get_from_http($project, $count, $user) // die "Could not get data from the server.\n";` — a single-caller pass-through — and get_from_http (lines 109-126) never reads $count: the request is `$url .= "/recent/$project/$user"` with no count parameter, and it already dies with a detailed message on failure, making run()'s `or die` and get_data's `// die` two extra error layers that can only fire when webclient->url is unset. The count WAS used by the old DB branch: reference/old_db/lib/App/Yath2/Command/recent.pm:104-119 had `get_from_db(...) || get_from_http(...)` with `rows => $count`; the #45 inlining (file header comment, lines 7-11) dropped the DB branch but kept the dead parameter. App::Yath2::Options::Recent is included ONLY here (`grep -rn "Options::Recent" lib t` → client/recent.pm:22 plus the module itself), so its `max` option (Options/Recent.pm:10) is user-visible with zero effect.
confirmedFindings.proposal: Either pass the count to the server (e.g. a ?count= query parameter) or stop including/computing it and drop the Options::Recent include if `max` cannot be honored over HTTP. Inline get_from_http's body into run() (or keep one method), collapsing the three stacked error paths into one.
confirmedFindings.accuracy_note: Minor mechanism imprecision (conclusion unaffected): the finding says both run()'s `or die` (line 59) and get_data's `// die` (line 106) "can only fire when webclient->url is unset." Only get_data's `// die` fires in the url-unset case (get_from_http returns undef there). run()'s `or die` is effectively unreachable: get_data either dies or returns get_from_http's value, so `or die` could only trigger on a defined-but-false decoded payload (e.g. JSON `0`/`""`), which then breaks the very next line `@$data = reverse @$data`. This makes run()'s `or die` even deader than described — it strengthens rather than weakens the "redundant stacked error paths" point.
confirmedFindings.value_note: Split the proposal and keep only the cheap, safe half. Do the CLIENT-side cleanup now: drop the dead `my $count = $recent->max || 10;` (line 56) and the `$count` argument threaded through get_data/get_from_http, and drop the `App::Yath2::Options::Recent` include (Options/Recent.pm:10) since `max` cannot be honored over the current HTTP endpoint. Optionally collapse get_data's pass-through `// die` into run() (one error layer), though that half is more cosmetic than load-bearing. DO NOT pursue the "pass ?count= to the server" alternative in this ticket — the web server that owns the `/recent/$project/$user` endpoint is being moved to reference/old_db and stubbed by #45, with no scheduled web-UI rewrite, so server-side count plumbing would be churn against soon-to-be-inert/rewritten code and should be deferred to whenever the web UI is rebuilt. Add a Depends/related note on #45 (DB-1): the client command lives alongside the now-inert `server`/`recent` DB stubs, so re-honoring `--max` over HTTP belongs to that future web rewrite, not now. Effort S / risk low is correct; note the one user-visible consequence is that `--max`/`--recent-max` disappears from `client-recent`, which is acceptable since it is currently a silent no-op.

confirmedFindings.title: Command/db/sync.pm and Command/import.pm duplicate the DB bootstrap scaffolding and the --to/--as-user option definitions
confirmedFindings.evidence: Both run() bodies contain the same block: `require App::Yath2::DB::Connect; require App::Yath2::Schema; require App::Yath2::DB::Sync;` then `my ($source_con) = App::Yath2::DB::Connect::build_connection($src, read_only => 1); my ($dest_con) = App::Yath2::DB::Connect::build_connection($to);` then `App::Yath2::DB::Sync->new(source => ..., dest => ..., as_user => ...)` (db/sync.pm:82-95 vs import.pm:78-93, including the same multi-line DuckDB read-only comment). The option groups also duplicate: `as_user` is defined twice with the same `from_env_vars => [qw/YATH_DB_AS_USER/]`, `alt => [qw/override-user/]` and near-identical description (db/sync.pm:43-48, import.pm:34-39), and `to` twice with the same description/examples (db/sync.pm:30-35, import.pm:27-32). The R11 lazy-require comment block is also repeated verbatim (db/sync.pm:17-20, import.pm:17-19).
confirmedFindings.proposal: Extract a small shared helper — e.g. App::Yath2::DB::Sync->connect_pair($from, $to) (or a function in DB::Connect) that does the requires + the read-only-source/writable-dest build_connection pair — and a shared option module (App::Yath2::Options::DBSync) contributing `to`/`as_user` so the descriptions and env vars are defined once.
confirmedFindings.accuracy_note: Three overstatements to correct, none of which invalidate the finding: (1) The DuckDB read-only comment is NOT "the same multi-line comment" — sync.pm:86-87 ("--from is read-only (Sync never writes the source). Mandatory for a DuckDB source...") and import.pm:82-85 ("The source is an existing log FILE/DSN (sqlite or duckdb, by extension)...") convey the same idea but are worded differently. (2) The R11 lazy-require comment is NOT "repeated verbatim" — the first two lines match, but sync.pm:19-20 adds an extra clause ("(App::Yath2::DB::Connect throws an actionable 'install ...' error when DBIx::QuickORM / the DBD driver is missing).") that import.pm:19 lacks (import.pm just ends "in run()."). (3) The proposal states a shared option module could define the `to` env vars "once," but the `to` env vars actually DIFFER between the two commands: YATH_DB_SYNC_TO (sync.pm:34) vs YATH_DB_IMPORT_TO (import.pm:31). Only description/examples for `to` are shareable; the env var must remain per-command (or be parameterized). The `as_user` env var (YATH_DB_AS_USER) genuinely is identical and fully shareable. Also note the settings group names differ (`sync` vs `import_db`, the latter documented as a deliberate workaround for Perl's universal import() method), so any shared helper reading settings must be given the resolved from/to/as_user values rather than reading a fixed group.
confirmedFindings.value_note: Narrow the proposal to its high-value half: the connect-pair helper (e.g. App::Yath2::DB::Sync->connect_pair($from, $to) or a DB::Connect function) doing the three requires + read-only-source/writable-dest build_connection pair, plus consolidating the R11 lazy-require and DuckDB read-only comments to one place. Downgrade the shared-option-module part: the finding overstates option identity — `to` uses different env vars (YATH_DB_SYNC_TO vs YATH_DB_IMPORT_TO) and `as_user` descriptions differ ("every synced run's..." vs "the imported run's..."), so a shared App::Yath2::Options::DBSync would have to parameterize env var + wording per command and may not net-simplify; only `as_user`'s shared bits (YATH_DB_AS_USER, override-user alt) are a clean common factor. Keep effort S, risk low. Add a Depends line to #53 and #54 (DB-5) since those tickets created and own these two commands; land the refactor after both are considered stable so it doesn't conflict with any in-flight DB-5 follow-up work.

confirmedFindings.title: _find_or_create is copy-pasted between DB::Logger and DB::Sync
confirmedFindings.evidence: Logger.pm:636 `sub _find_or_create ($self, $table, $natural, $pk_col) { my $con = $self->con; my $row = $con->handle($table, where => $natural)->first; return $row->field($pk_col) if $row; my $new = $con->handle($table)->insert($natural); return $new->field($pk_col); }` and Sync.pm:448 are identical except for the connection source ($self->con vs $self->{+DEST}). This is the natural-key find_or_create primitive the whole R5 design leans on (Logger uses it for hosts/machine_users/projects/test_files; Sync for every remap), so a behavior fix (e.g. handling an insert race between two loggers) currently has to be made twice.
confirmedFindings.proposal: Move it to one shared home that both use — e.g. `App::Yath2::DB::Connect::find_or_create($con, $table, $natural, $pk_col)` (Connect is already the common runtime dep of both) — and have Logger/Sync call it with their connection.
confirmedFindings.accuracy_note: Minor: the two bodies are functionally identical but not textually verbatim — the local variable is named $con in Logger and $dest in Sync, and the connection is reached differently (an accessor `$self->con` vs a direct hash-slot `$self->{+DEST}`). Any shared helper must therefore take the connection object as an explicit argument (as the proposal already suggests), rather than being a straight lift of the method. Effort/risk (S/low) are reasonable.

confirmedFindings.title: client/publish.pm is the only code in the distribution using LWP::UserAgent, loaded at compile time, while every other HTTP consumer uses lazily-required HTTP::Tiny
confirmedFindings.evidence: `grep -rln "LWP::UserAgent|HTTP::Tiny" lib` shows client/publish.pm is the sole LWP user; its sibling client/recent.pm (`require HTTP::Tiny;` at line 115), Finder.pm:150, Plugin/Notify.pm:300, Plugin/YathUI.pm:211 and Util/JSON.pm:121 all lazily require HTTP::Tiny. Also drop the redundant compile-time `use LWP;` (line 12) alongside `use LWP::UserAgent;` and make the load lazy (eval/require) to match every other HTTP consumer. Scope note for a Depends line: independent of the DB chunks (#45-#56) — can land anytime, no ordering constraint. Caveat worth recording: publish.pm's target web server moves to reference/old_db and is stubbed under #45, so the command is effectively dormant until the deferred future webapp-port spec (which may rewrite publish entirely); therefore frame the concrete, near-term value as removing the LWP::UserAgent hard dependency rather than user-facing behavior — that value stands regardless of the webapp port's eventual outcome.
