confirmedFindings.title: Three near-duplicate cwd-to-root directory walks in App::Yath2::Util, two with identical loop skeletons
confirmedFindings.evidence: find_in_updir (125-139), _find_link_in_updir (156-172), and _glob_runner_links_updir (343-356) all implement 'walk from cwd upward with a %seen guard until the filesystem root'. _find_link_in_updir and _glob_runner_links_updir are byte-for-byte the same skeleton — `my $dir = eval { realpath(File::Spec->rel2abs('.')) } or return; while (defined $dir && length $dir && !$seen{$dir}++) { ...per-level action...; my $parent = realpath(File::Spec->catdir($dir, '..')) // last; last if $parent eq $dir; $dir = $parent; }` — differing only in the per-level body (first -l match vs collect glob results). find_in_updir implements the same walk a third, different way (accumulating '../..' relative paths), so the one concept has two coexisting mechanics.
confirmedFindings.proposal: Extract a private _walk_updirs($per_dir_cb) helper that owns the realpath/%seen/parent/root loop; the three functions become one-line-body callers (return-first vs collect). Also lets find_in_updir share the same, safer realpath-parent mechanics.
confirmedFindings.accuracy_note: Two accuracy caveats for whoever acts on this: (1) The two link-walkers are the clean extract-a-callback case; find_in_updir is a weaker merge candidate because its %seen guard keys on the resolved full path ($check, which includes the final path component) rather than the directory ($dir), and it seeds by prepending '..' to the target path rather than realpath'ing the cwd — so folding it into a shared _walk_updirs($per_dir_cb) helper is not purely mechanical and must preserve that keying/termination difference. (2) _find_link_in_updir exists separately from find_in_updir on purpose (see the comment at 152-155: realpath follows the symlink to its socket target, so it can't match a link), so the helper must expose the raw $dir to the callback rather than a realpath'd final path — the proposal's callback shape already accommodates this, but it's the load-bearing constraint.

confirmedFindings.title: Event fan-out still lives in legacy Renderer::Base, forcing every loop-era engine through a dispatch_cb redirect plus a dummy `renderers => []`, while Command::stop still uses the pre-RenderLoop direct path

Two evidence details are imprecise but do not sink the finding:

More importantly, dist.ini's [GatherDir] does NOT exclude AI_DOCS/ (its exclude_match list covers reference, demo, xt/downstream, pt, tt, release-scripts, cover, nyt, test-logs, t/, t2/, old/ — but not AI_DOCS). 2) The STYLE_GUIDE AI_DOCS prohibition is literally scoped to comments and POD, not to arbitrary user-facing strings; the finding is applying the guide's intent (which it openly states as "the same intent applies"), not citing a literal rule violation. confirmedFindings.title: stop.pm decides control flow by testing $@ instead of the eval return value, and omits the ;1 success sentinel
confirmedFindings.evidence: Lines 53-54: `my $render = eval { $self->prime_shutdown };` then `warn "Could not prime runner shutdown renderer: $@" unless defined $render || !$@;`. This violates the STYLE_GUIDE mandate to always check the eval return (`my $ok = eval { ...; 1 }`), not $@. The eval omits the `; 1` success sentinel, so a legitimate `return undef` from prime_shutdown (line 96, when runner output is hidden) is indistinguishable from a failure by $render alone; success/failure is disambiguated only via a direct $@ test. The rest of the same sub (lines 60, 65, 69) correctly uses `my $ok = eval { ...; 1 }`.
confirmedFindings.proposal: Restructure as the mandated three-step / capture form, e.g. `my $ok = eval { $render = $self->prime_shutdown; 1 }; my $err = $@; warn "Could not prime runner shutdown renderer: $err" unless $ok;` so the success decision rides the eval return.
confirmedFindings.accuracy_note: Minor context, not a refutation: the code is functionally correct today because a successful eval resets `$@` to '' (so a legit `return undef` with empty `$@` suppresses the warn). The defect is that it violates the documented mandate and carries the exact latent fragility the guide warns about — `$@` can be clobbered during stack unwinding (e.g. a DESTROY handler) between the eval and the test — not that it misbehaves in the common case. Severity is style/maintainability (category "inconsistency" is apt), not an active runtime bug. The proposed three-step/capture rewrite is correct.
